ITEM.PTXT: A fuel returnless system has been adopted for excellent emission performance.
The fuel tank capacity is 60L.
A resin fuel delivery pipe has been adopted to reduce weight.
Quick connectors have been adopted at each connection of the fuel pipes to improve serviceability.
A fuel pump integrated with the charcoal canister, fuel filter, etc. has been adopted, reducing weight and saving space in the engine room.

A fixed-torque type fuel tank cap, which cannot be tightened further once tightened a certain amount, has been adopted. This reduces the operating force of the fuel tank cap, ensuring excellent operability.
By adopting an air filter at the mouth of the fuel tank inlet pipe, underfloor space has been secured.

The pressure regulator integrated with the fuel pump returns fuel within the fuel tank, supplying only the amount consumed by the engine at a constant fuel pressure. As a result, fuel heated while passing through the engine room does not return to the fuel tank, suppressing the generation of evaporative gas in the fuel tank for excellent emission performance.
A fuel tank with a capacity of 60L has been installed under the floor of the first and second seats, achieving a spacious interior.
The material is aluminum-plated steel sheet, and the use of lead has been eliminated in consideration of environmental impact.
A fuel drain mark has been provided on the bottom surface of the fuel tank to clarify and simplify positioning of the fuel draining device during dismantling and to ensure reliable fuel draining.
By adopting an aluminum heat insulator, fuel temperature rise has been suppressed and weight has been reduced.
A circumferential flow type in-tank fuel pump has been adopted.
By integrating the charcoal canister, fuel filter, pressure regulator and fuel sender gauge into the fuel pump assembly, weight has been reduced and space in the engine room has been saved.

In the saddle type tank, when the remaining fuel becomes low, the tank is divided into 2 chambers, A and B, and fuel remains in chamber B. The jet pump uses the flow velocity of the return fuel in the fuel tank to draw up fuel by the vacuum generated when it passes through the venturi, transferring fuel from chamber B to chamber A.

To accurately inform the driver of the remaining fuel in the saddle type tank, sender gauges are provided in series in the 2 chambers, A and B. The remaining fuel in both chambers is output to the meter computer.
The remaining fuel (remaining fuel signal) from the variable resistor of the fuel sender gauge is input to the meter computer, which calculates the remaining fuel display data.
A resin delivery pipe has been adopted to reduce weight.
The left and right fuel delivery pipes are connected by a nylon tube.
A fuel pulsation damper is provided on the right bank fuel delivery pipe to suppress fuel pulsation, stabilizing the air-fuel ratio and reducing noise.

A 12-hole ultra-fine atomization fuel injector has been adopted. The injector is mounted directly on the cylinder head, and the tip of the fuel injector protrudes into the intake port, shortening the distance to the combustion chamber. This reduces fuel adhesion to the intake port, achieving low fuel consumption and low emissions.
Canister purge control, which draws fuel evaporative gas generated from the fuel tank into the intake port and burns it, has been adopted.
Integrated with the fuel pump and located inside the fuel tank. As a result, the fuel system has been made lighter and more compact.
The canister purge volume is controlled by the signal (duty signal) from the engine control computer. The purge volume is determined by the ratio of the ON and OFF times of the signal (duty ratio).
